title: Decode: KDA core (FP32 state)
shape: NVFP4 1-node D3-32 DP-rank slice (L24 view), r24 (384 verify rows), u132k, k=3; ms per decode step
basis: MEASURED in-step NVFP4 baseline (INFRA 18:52 EST, measured/20261118-1900-nvfp4-decode.json); achievable = nvfp4_modelopt at the same slice
gap_analysis: MEASURED (runs/D-KDA run2/run3, 1-GPU microbench at the D3-32 per-GPU shape, deferred fold active): KdaWide n32/64/96/128 = 26.0/51.5/74.3/95.0 us/layer, KdaWS (no fold; flush pass extra) 20.5/37.4/48.5/62.3; state stream only 3-6.5 TB/s and a 2-page state ring changes nothing -> not bandwidth / bytes-in-flight bound. In-kernel clock64 trace of KdaFlow (WS + fold) at n96: the 8-warp scan is the bottleneck (verify ~5.5-7K cycles/item vs ~2.5K FP32-pipe floor, fold ~3.5-4.5K/item vs ~1K), scan waits ~0 on the state and ~13% on prep; prep body ~8K cycles/item per warpgroup (global round trips: F_B tile loads, old records, weights), so prep is the next limit once the scan speeds up. Root cause: latency-bound dependency chain per token (k-dot reduce -> v -> update -> q-dot reduce) with only 2 scan warps per SMSP, plus global-latency-bound prep.
inefficiencies: MEASURED: KdaFlow scan fold and verify each ~9K cycles/item at n96 (instruction floor ~1-2K): suspect register cap 128 + local-memory stack (STACK 88) in the fused fold+verify scan
MEASURED: prep + state load floor 32 us/layer at n96 (~7K cycles/item, 2 prep warpgroups): above the model target on its own
MEASURED: KdaWS (production n>=71) does not fold: extra flush pass (state R+W) on top of 48.5 us/layer
MEASURED: HBM only 3-6.5 TB/s in every variant: not bandwidth bound; die-local streaming premature
rubin_features: two-die locality domains: per-4 KiB page home die (default interleave) + %smid -> die map (dies.py)
bulk async copies (TMA) into a multi-stage shared-memory ring
plan: SOL DESIGN (KdaFlow v3, one persistent kernel, one state pass): per SM two independent scan groups (4 warps each, 128 threads, thread = 8 rows x 16 keys, 128 FP32 state regs, same per-row partial/butterfly tree as KdaWS so bitwise parity holds) run two items concurrently so one group's reduction/broadcast latency hides under the other's FP32 passes; fold (stock commit association) + verify + gated o_norm per item from registers; folded state written straight from registers (coalesced 128 B rows, evict-first); state pages bulk-copied into a per-group smem slot as soon as the group has the previous page in registers (2 x 64 KiB in flight per SM); one prep warpgroup with no global round trips in its body (per-head conv/F_B/dt constants cached: F_B for the CTA's <=2 heads staged once in smem; per-item rows, conv window, old records cp.async-staged one item ahead).

Bound resources at n96 (per SM, ~10.9 items): FP32 pipe ~3K cycles/item (fold ~7.8 + verify 16 FP32 ops per state element, FFMA2) = ~14 us; state R+W 302 MB at the striped HBM rate ~22-24 us -> memory bound, projected ~24-26 us/layer (x69 = 1.7-1.8 ms) vs model achievable 26.3 us (1.81 ms), target 28.9 us (1.99 ms).
Step 1: implement v3 in cutedsl/kda/flow.py (replaces v1/v2), bitwise test vs KdaWS triton + stock commit, microbench n32/64/96/128.
Step 2: if FP/prep bound: clock64 trace per role; tune groups/regs; if memory bound below target: 2-stage ring per group (oversized smem) / die-local state placement.
Step 3: dispatch flow for the measured winning n range (RECORD_KINDS), in-step slice A/B on the int overlay, landed-ready.
